writeup.headline: Netskope pairs 30% growth and net cash with deep losses, heavy dilution and a high sales multiple: Hold.
writeup.thesis: Netskope rates Hold with a composite score of 50, as strong growth, a solid balance sheet and powerful price momentum are offset by weak quality and a very low valuation score. Growth scores 80 on TTM revenue growth of 30.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 29.1% year on year, with growth sped up by 1.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores only 19: the gross margin is 69.9%, but the operating margin is -94.7%, the FCF margin is -8.7%, stock-based compensation equals 79.4% of revenue, and the diluted share count is up 274.7% year on year. The balance sheet scores 96 on cash-to-debt of 1.53, with net cash and 15.2 years of cash at the current burn. Valuation scores 4: P/S of 13.4x is high in absolute terms and the FCF yield is 5.6 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, while trend (76) reflects the price at its 52-week high and 102.6% above its 200-day average.
key_risks: Deep operating losses and stock-based compensation at 79.4% of revenue, with the diluted share count up 274.7% year on year.
A high absolute sales multiple of 13.4x leaves little room for any growth slowdown.
The price is 48.0% above its 50-day average and 102.6% above its 200-day average after a sharp run, so a pullback could be steep.
The Fortinet patent suit remains unresolved.
Free cash flow is still negative, so the business relies on its cash pile until it turns profitable.
what_would_change: The score is 6 points above the Sell band, so a fading trend score or a growth slowdown could push it to Sell.
Reaching Buy needs 15 more points, most plausibly from better quality: narrower operating losses, positive free cash flow and much lower dilution.
A lower share price or faster revenue growth that brings P/S down from 13.4x would lift the valuation score from 4.
Negative news, such as a guidance cut or an adverse outcome in the Fortinet suit, would weigh on the news score of 59.
